text:
sam: Quick intake — kelvin11b bring-up econ vs quality. I pushed microbench + eval slices to the shared drive. TL;DR: fp16 baseline p50=13ms, p95=48ms, 120 tps, est cost $3.2 / 1M tokens. int8 (q4f16) p50=9ms, p95=65ms, 170 tps, est cost $1.9 / 1M. Quality: int8 shows ~2.3% avg drop on longform R@5 and some hallucination deltas on instruction-following slices. Need recommendation for GTN/product defaults + rollout plan.

anya: saw the artifacts. nice work. quick thoughts: 2.3% drop is within our usual acceptable band for low-cost GTN surfaces but not for core search/rerank. propose two defaults: 1) cost-sensitive: kelvin11b-int8 w/ prefix-cache and token-budgeting; 2) fidelity-sensitive: kelvin11b-fp16. Use hybrid routing based on prompt length & feature flag. :thinking_face:

liam: ops note — int8 tail (p95->p99) balloons under burst due to slower kv-cache priming in current runtime. numbers from canary: int8 p99=210ms vs fp16 p99=120ms. That's customer-visible. If we route short queries to int8 but a user sends long context it might cross the p95 threshold. Need a fallback policy and canary rollout with traffic ramp.

jin: agree with anya on hybrid. additional experiments I'd run before-wide rollout: (a) per-layer groupwise int6 sweep (b) 4-bit QAT demo on representative eval slices (c) temperature + beam ablation to quantify hallucination delta. Also add synthetic adversarial slices focused on longform coherence. We should quantify tradeoff in units: cost per request vs drop in R@5.

perf-bot: microbench summary from canary run (timestamps in artifacts): model=kelvin11b, config=int8-q4f16, batch=8, seq=512 -> p50=9ms, p95=65ms, p99=210ms, tps=170. fp16 batch=8 seq=512 -> p50=13ms, p95=48ms, p99=120ms, tps=120. unit_econ_estimate: int8 $1.9/1M, fp16 $3.2/1M. perf-bot: added link -> https://drive.redwood/kelvin11b/canary_3899999999/

sam: ok — product asks: what should we set as default for new GTN customers? and what rollout policy do you recommend (canary %, metrics to watch, fallback triggers)?

anya: recommendation: default = kelvin11b-int8 for new cost-sensitive GTN tiers. Flag: `model=kelvin11b:variant=int8` behind a feature flag `kelvin11b-default-int8`. Rollout: canary 5% x 24h, 25% x 48h, 100% if no regressions. Metrics to watch: p95 latency, p99 latency, R@5 on the product slice, hallucination-rate on the longform slice, error-rate. Fallback triggers: if p95 > 120ms OR R@5 drop > 3% absolute OR error-rate increased by 0.5pp -> automatic fallback to fp16 route.

liam: add ops checklist: 1) enable prefix KV warmstart for int8 priming; 2) ensure routing policy respects context-length (route if context_len > 2048 -> fp16); 3) retry budget 2 + jitter; 4) alert on queue length > 50 per worker. Also add a gradual CPU/GPU mem monitor.

jin: experiment plan (short): run 10k eval queries across product GTN slices for int8, int6-gw, int4-qat. Collect R@1/5, BLEU-like coherence, hallucination markers, latency tails. Post results as a tiny scorecard. If int6 hits cost ~1.5/1M with <2% quality drop we pick that for cost tier.

sam: can someone drop a rollout config snippet I can hand to SRE? I'll create the feature flag and ship the canary.

anya: snippet below — replace placeholders. use canary flag + fallback policy.

anya: ```
# rollout config
model: "kelvin11b"
variant: "int8"
feature_flag: "kelvin11b-default-int8"
canary: [ {percent:5, duration:"24h"}, {percent:25, duration:"48h"} ]
fallback: {
  conditions: ["p95_latency>120ms", "r5_drop_abs>0.03", "error_rate_increase>0.005"],
  action: "route->kelvin11b-fp16"
}
monitoring: ["p50","p95","p99","r5_product_slice","hallucination_rate"]
```

liam: :thumbsup: will wire alerts. sam I added the drive links to the canary run in the ticket.

sam: thanks all. next steps: jin to run int6 + int4 sweep (end of week), anya to draft scorecard template, liam to prep rollout alerts & prefix warmstart. we'll reconvene after 10k-slice run. :rocket:
